claims.claim: The WHO estimates occupational asbestos exposure causes more than 200,000 deaths worldwide each year.
claims.episode_span: Estimates from the World Health Organization suggest that occupational asbestos exposure still claims more than 200,000 lives worldwide each year
claims.source_title: Asbestos - World Health Organization fact sheet
claims.supporting_quote: exposure to asbestos at work causes more than 200 000 deaths globally every year (based on estimates for 2016). This represents over 70% of deaths from work-related cancers.

claims.claim: A 1960 paper by Wagner and colleagues, based on South African cases, established the link between asbestos exposure and mesothelioma.
claims.episode_span: Researchers in South Africa finally tied crocidolite asbestos to mesothelioma clusters, yet widespread use continued for another decade.
claims.supporting_quote: In 1960, an article published by Wagner et al. was seminal in establishing mesothelioma as a disease arising from exposure to asbestos.

claims.claim: A 1924 publication by Dr. W. E. Cooke described the first medical-literature case of death from pulmonary asbestosis (textile worker Nellie Kershaw).
claims.episode_span: a 1924 study by Dr. W. E. Cooke that named asbestosis, described lung scarring
claims.supporting_quote: The death of English textile worker Nellie Kershaw in 1924 from pulmonary asbestosis was the first case to be described in medical literature, and the first published account of disease definitely attributed to occupational asbestos exposure.

claims.claim: An early-1900s British medical report (H. Montague Murray's 1906 testimony, published 1907) linked asbestos dust to fatal lung fibrosis in an asbestos worker.
claims.episode_span: including a 1907 British report on asbestos-factory workers
claims.supporting_quote: testified before a British committee concerning a patient who died in April 1900. Murray indicated that fibrosis of the lungs caused by asbestos dust was a plausible cause of the patient's death.

claims.claim: Johns-Manville filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 1982 under asbestos injury liability.
claims.episode_span: leading to the bankruptcy of Johns-Manville in 1982
claims.supporting_quote: In 1982, facing unprecedented liability for asbestos injury claims, the company voluntarily filed for bankruptcy under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.
